reason: H0 fuzzes only HTTP bytes after constructing a fixed configuration with small hard-coded timeout values. It never fuzzes the scalar configuration paths changed in S1, including zero and extreme uint64_t timeout values. Those inputs control disabled-versus-immediate semantics, unchecked multiplication by 1000 in config_timeout, timer expiration arithmetic in h2o_timer_now_plus, and the range rejection in h2o_timer_add_. This is a distinct fuzz-worthy configuration and timer-boundary surface not reachable from Data in H0.
evidence: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput passes Data only to create_accepted and feeder as request bytes.

H0 assigns config.http2.idle_timeout, config.http1.req_timeout, config.proxy.io_timeout, config.proxy.connect_timeout, and config.proxy.first_byte_timeout to fixed values during one-time initialization.
lib/core/configurator.c::config_timeout accepts a SCNu64 scalar and assigns timeout_in_secs * 1000 without a visible overflow check.
The proxy and FastCGI configure_timer functions accept arbitrary SCNu64 values, while on_config_websocket_timeout independently accepts an arbitrary SCNu64 timeout.

S1 changes h2o_timer_val_t and h2o_timer_abs_t to raw uint64_t values, makes zero the unset/disabled representation in checks such as h2o_socketpool_can_keepalive, and performs timeout + h2o_now(loop) in h2o_timer_now_plus.
h2o_timer_add_ rejects expirations more than 0xffffffff beyond last_run, but H0 does not derive timer values from fuzz input.
recommended_action: Add a configuration/timer fuzz target that feeds generated scalar values through config_timeout, the proxy and FastCGI timeout configurators, and on_config_websocket_timeout, emphasizing 0, 1, values around UINT64_MAX/1000, UINT64_MAX, and expirations around last_run + 0xffffffff; then initialize/run the affected timer, proxy, socket-pool, and FastCGI paths.
